title: ontology_DAG: a class for ontology data
text: DAG object constructed via list parent-child pairs. following code constructs DAG diagram . Typing dag prints basic information DAG. Aspect ratio calculated width/height, width largest number terms specific depth (.e. max(table(depth(dag)))). Definition height term DAG depends whether using longest shortest distance root. aspect ratio gives impression shape DAG looks like (fat slim). ontology_DAG object can also constructed vector parent-child links: Following functions return root term, leaf terms test whether terms leaves. dag_all_terms() returns vector terms. dag_n_terms() simply returns number terms DAG.

title: ontology_DAG: a class for ontology data
text: depth term defined longest distance root calculated dag_depth(). want shortest distance root, use dag_shortest_dist_from_root(). Similarly, “height” term defined longest distance reachable leaf terms. dag_shortest_dist_to_leaves() returns shortest distance leaves. four functions introduced far calculate distance root leaves terms DAG. following functions general calculates distance self-defined group terms group terms. dag_depth() identical dag_longest_dist_to_offspring(dag, root), dag_height() identical dag_longest_dist_from_ancestors(dag, leaves) root single root term leaves vector leaf terms DAG. Please note, four functions applied terms. return vector length total terms DAG. term included calculation, e.g. root term include , dag_longest_dist_to_offspring() dag_shortest_dist_to_offspring() assign -1 root term. Given two terms DAG, following four functions calculate pair-wise distance. different ways calculate distance: two terms \(\) \(b\), shortest_distances_via_NCA() calculates distance : \[ \min_{t \\mathrm{CA}(, b)}(D_{sp}(t, ) + D_{sp}(t, b)) \] \(\mathrm{CA}(, b)\) set common ancestors (CA) \(\) \(b\). \(D_{sp}(x, y)\) shortest distance \(x\) \(y\). way, common ancestor \(t\) returns minimal distance \(\) \(b\) called “nearest common ancestor (NCA)” \(\) \(b\). usage function follows. returns symmetric matrix pair-wise distance terms. longest_distances_via_LCA() calculates distance : \[ \mathrm{len}(t, ) + \mathrm{len}(t, b) \] \(\mathrm{len}(x, y)\) longest distance \(x\) \(y\). Common ancestor \(t\) one largest depth DAG called lowest common ancestor (LCA) \(\) \(b\): \[ t = \operatorname*{argmax}_{t \\mathrm{CA}(, b)} \delta(t)\] \(\delta(t)\) depth (maximal distance root) term \(t\). usage function : next two functions treat DAG relations directional. positive distance value term ancestor , else distance set -1 returned distance matrix.

text: Terms can external items annotated. One typical example GO terms can genes annotated. Later annotated items can used calculating semantic similarities. annotation set list character vectors, names element vectors correspond term names DAG annotations can mapped terms. Due nature DAG, child term annotated item, ancestor terms also associated item. calculation annotated items applied recursive way. term \(x\), denote \(\mathcal{C}_x\) set child terms, items “directly” annotated \(x\) denoted set \(G^*_x\), final set items annotated \(x\) denoted \(G_x\) union items annotated child terms well \(x\) . \[ G_x = \left( \bigcup_{z \\mathcal{C}_x} G_z \right) \bigcup G^*_x \] Note equation applied resursively. denoting \(\mathcal{D}^+_x\) set \(x\)’s offspring terms plus \(x\) , \(G^*_x\) can also written : \[ G_x = \bigcup_{z \\mathcal{D}^+_x} G_z^* \] numbers annotated items DAG terms can obtained via function n_annotations(). attribute attr(,"N") maximal number items annotated DAG (max(n_annotations(dag))), normally corresponds root term. next two functions return associations terms items. return binary matrix:

text: measures probability term getting full transmission root. term associated p-value root p-value 1. understand method, let’s think DAG relates kind information transmission root inner DAG, information 100% root. , certain level DAG, term \(x\) two parents \(t_1\) \(t_2\), also let’s assume \(t_1\) \(k_1\) children \(t_2\) \(k_2\) children, next assume parent transmits information equally children, \(t_1\) transmits \(1/k_1\) \(t_2\) transmits \(1/k_2\) content term \(x\), also say, probability \(t_1\) \(t_2\) reach \(x\) \(1/k_1\) \(1/k_2\). Let’s assume \(p(t_1)\) \(p(t_2)\) accumulated contents root \(t_1\) \(t_2\) already (probability two parent terms getting full transmission root), probability reaching \(x\) via full transmission graph \(t_1\) multiplication \(p(t_1)\) \(1/k_1\), \(p(t_1)/k_1\), similar \(p(t_2)/k_2\). , term \(x\), getting transmitted \(t_1\) \(t_2\) independent, probability \(x\) (denoted \(p(x)\)) get transmitted parents : \[ p(x) = \frac{p(t_1)}{k_1} * \frac{p(t_2)}{k_2} \] Since two parents full set \(x\)’s parents, \(p(x)\) probability \(x\) getting full transmission root. final information content : \[ \mathrm{IC}(x) = -\log(p(x)) \] formal definition : \[ p(x) = \left\{ \begin{array}{cl} 1 & \text{} \textit{x} \text{ root} \\ \prod\limits_{t \\mathcal{P}_x} \frac{p(t)}{|\mathcal{C}_t|} & \text{otherwise} \end{array} \right. \] Paper link: https://doi.org/10.1155/2012/975783.

title: Information content
text: based number offspring terms () term \(x\). information content calculated : \[  \begin{align*} \mathrm{IC}(x) & = \frac{\log(\frac{|\mathcal{D}_x^+|}{|\mathcal{D}_r^+|})}{\log(\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_r^+|})}  \\  & = 1 - \frac{\log(|\mathcal{D}_x^+|)}{\log(|\mathcal{D}_r^+|)} \end{align*}  \] \(|\mathcal{D}_r^+|\) total number terms DAG. IC_Seco_2004 actually normalized version IC_offspring: \[ \begin{align*} \mathrm{IC}_\mathrm{Seco}(x) & = 1 - \frac{\log(|\mathcal{D}_x^+|)}{\log(|\mathcal{D}_r^+|)} \\ & = \frac{\log(|\mathcal{D}_r^+|) - \log(|\mathcal{D}_x^+|)}{\log(|\mathcal{D}_r^+|)} \\ & = \frac{-\log (|\mathcal{D}_x^+| / |\mathcal{D}_r^+|)}{-\log(1/|\mathcal{D}_r^+|)} \\ & = \frac{\mathrm{IC}_\mathrm{offspring}(x)}{\mathrm{IC}_\mathrm{offspring}^\mathrm{max}} \end{align*} \] \(\mathrm{IC}_\mathrm{offspring}^\mathrm{max} = -\log(1/|\mathcal{D}_r^+|)\) leaf terms (\(|\mathcal{D}_\mathrm{leaf}^+| = 1\)). DAG tree structure, .e. term one parent root parent, following relation: \[ \lambda_\mathrm{node} = \lambda_\mathrm{edge} + 1\] case, \(\sigma \approx 0.5\), \[ \mathrm{IC}(x) = 0.5 * \mathrm{IC}_\mathrm{Seco}(x) + 0.5 * \frac{\log(\lambda(x)+1)}{\log(\lambda_\mathrm{edge}+1)} \] Paper link: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.5555/1862330.1862343.

Paper link: http://article.nadiapub.com/IJGDC/vol5_no3/6.pdf.

title: Information content
text: child-parent relation weighted value smaller 1 based semantic relation type, .e. 0.8 “is_a” 0.6 “part_of”. term \(x\) one ancestor term \(t\), first calculates “S-value” corresponds path \(t\) \(x\) accumulated multiplication weights along path reaches maximal: \[ S_x(t) = \left\{ \begin{array}{cl} 1 & \text{} \textit{t = x} \\ \max\limits_{t' \\mathcal{C}_t}{w_e * S_x(t')} & \text{otherwise} \end{array} \right. \] properly understand setting, let’s first apply following transformation: \[ T_x(t) = \log(1/S_x(t)) \] definition \(S_x(t)\) converted \(T_x(t)\): \[ T_x(t) = \left\{ \begin{array}{cl} 0 & \text{} \textit{t = x} \\ \min\limits_{t' \\mathcal{C}_t}{\frac{1}{w_e} * T_x(t')} & \text{otherwise} \end{array} \right. \] way, \(T_x(t)\) actually shortest distance \(t\) \(x\) taking \(1/w_e\) edge weight. can obtain \(S_x(t)\) back : \[ S_x(t) = \exp(-T_x(t)) \] information content summation \(x\)’s ancestors: \[ \mathrm{IC}(x) = \sum\limits_{t \\mathcal{}_x^+} S_x(t) \] Normally IC_Wang_2007 used calculating semantic similarity using Sim_Wang_2007 method. contribution different semantic relations can set contribution_factor parameter. value named numeric vector names cover relations defined relations set create_ontology_DAG(). example, two relations “relation_a” “relation_b” set DAG, value contribution_factor can set : default 0.8 set “is_a” 0.6 “part_of”. sure types relations set, simply type dag object. relation types printed . title: Term similarity
text: term \(x\), first calculates “mile-stone” value based depth \[ m(x) = 2^{-\delta(x) - 1} \] distance bewteen term \(\) \(b\) via LCA term \(c\) : \[  \begin{align*} D(, b) & = D(c, ) + D(c, b) \\    & = m(c) - m() + m(c) + m(b) \\    & = 2^{-\delta(c)} - 2^{-\delta() - 1} - 2^{-\delta(b) - 1} \end{align*} \] can change original \(\delta()\) \(\delta(b)\) \(\delta_c()\) \(\delta_c(b)\) require depth reach \(\) \(b\) go \(c\). equation becomes \[  \begin{align*} D(, b) & = 2^{-\delta(c)} - 2^{-\delta_c() - 1} - 2^{-\delta_c(b) - 1} \\     & = 2^{-\delta(c)} - 2^{-\delta(c)-\mathrm{len}(c,)-1} - 2^{-\delta(c)-\mathrm{len}(c,b)-1} \\     & = 2^{-\delta(c)} \left( 1 - 2^{-\mathrm{len}(c,)-1} - 2^{-\mathrm{len}(c,b)-1} \right) \end{align*} \] \(= b\) (two terms identical), \(D(, b) = 0\) \(c = r\) (common ancestor includes root) \(\mathrm{len}(r, ) \\infty\), \(\mathrm{len}(r, b) \\infty\) (root infinite distance terms), \(D(, b)\) reaches maximal 1. similarity \[ \mathrm{Sim}(, b) = 1 - D(, b)\] ranges 0 1. text: definition kappa coeffient little bit complex. First let’s format two sets contigency table: \(\), \(b\), \(c\), \(d\) numbers items fall category. Let’s calculate \(p_\mathrm{obs}\) (probability observed agreement, yes ) \(p_\mathrm{exp}\) (probability expected agreement) : \[ \begin{align*} p_\mathrm{obs} & = \frac{+d}{+b+c+d} \\ p_\mathrm{Yes} & = \frac{+b}{+b+c+d} * \frac{+c}{+b+c+d} \\ p_\mathrm{} & = \frac{c+d}{+b+c+d} * \frac{b+d}{+b+c+d} \\ p_\mathrm{exp} & = p_\mathrm{Yes} + p_\mathrm{} \end{align*} \] \(p_\mathrm{obs}\) probability item sets neither sets, \(p_\mathrm{Yes}\) probability item sets random (assuming events item set \(\) set \(B\) independent), \(p_\mathrm{}\) probability item two sets random, \(p_\mathrm{exp}\) probability item either two sets two sets random. kappa coeffcient calculated : \[ \mathrm{Sim}(, b) = \mathrm{Kappa}(, b) = \frac{p_\mathrm{obs} - p_\mathrm{exp}}{1 - p_\mathrm{exp}}\] Note Kappa coeffcient possible negative. universe set can set via parameter anno_universe. default total items annotated whole DAG.

Dot size corresponds number child terms. default, DAG cut root term, sub-DAG assigned different color. Child terms root added legend plot. “name” column meta data frame, texts “name” column used legend labels, else term IDs used. default DAG split certain level controlled argument partition_by_level. can also controlled setting possible number terms sub-DAG.  dag_treelize() can convert DAG tree term one parent. circular visualization reduced tree follows:  One useful application map GO terms interest (e.g. significant GO terms function enrichment analysis) DAG. following example, go_tb contains GO terms enrichment analysis.  next example, map -log10(p.adjust) node size. dag_circular_viz() node_size argument allows set node sizes terms, thus, need calculate node sizes adjusted p-values. following code, defined simple node_size_fun() function linearly interpolates values node sizes within [2, 10]. also generate legend node sizes: Calculate node sizes: finally make circular plot:
code: dag_circular_viz(dag) dag_circular_viz(dag, partition_by_size = 5000) tree = dag_treelize(dag) dag_circular_viz(tree) go_tb = readRDS(system.file("extdata", "sig_go_tb.rds", package = "simona")) sig_go_ids = go_tb$ID[go_tb$p.adjust < 0.01] # make sure `sig_go_ids` all in current GO.db version sig_go_ids = intersect(sig_go_ids, dag_all_terms(dag)) dag_circular_viz(dag, highlight = sig_go_ids) p.adjust = go_tb$p.adjust[go_tb$p.adjust < 0.01] node_size_fun = function(x, range = c(2, 10)) {     s = (range[2] - range[1])/(quantile(x, 0.95) - min(x)) * (x - min(x)) + range[1]     s[s > range[2]] = range[2]     s } library(ComplexHeatmap) lgd = Legend(title = "p.adjust", at = -log10(c(0.01, 0.001, 0.0001)),      labels = c("0.01", "0.001", "0.0001"), type = "points",     size = unit(node_size_fun(-log10(c(0.01, 0.001, 0.0001))), "pt")) node_size = rep(2, dag_n_terms(dag)) names(node_size) = dag_all_terms(dag) node_size[sig_go_ids] = node_size_fun(-log10(p.adjust)) dag_circular_viz(dag,      highlight = sig_go_ids,     node_size = node_size,     edge_transparency = 0.92,      other_legends = lgd)

text: following three types common ancestors: MICA (informative common ancestor): common ancestor highest IC value.
